git.title: Git is a product name. Used as the title of the panel and of error dialogs.
git.scopeTitle: Tooltip explaining that the collection folder is only a part of a bigger repository.
git.tabs.changes: Tab with the list of modified files.
git.tabs.branches: Tab with the list of Git branches.
git.tabs.stashes: Tab with stashes: changes set aside temporarily.
git.tabs.history: Tab with the list of commits.
git.tabs.remotes: Tab with remote repositories, such as the one on GitHub.
git.fetch: Git command name. Many translations keep the English word.
git.pull: Git command: download and merge changes.
git.pullBehind: {{count}} is the number of commits that can be pulled.
git.pushAhead: {{count}} is the number of commits that can be pushed.
git.fetchedBehind: Output line after fetch. {{count}} commits are available to pull.
git.pushedTo: {{upstream}} is the name of the remote branch.
git.sectionTitle: Heading of a list with the number of entries, for example "Changes (3)".
git.sections.conflicts: Heading of files with merge conflicts.
git.sections.staged: Heading of files added to the next commit.
git.stageAll: Button that adds every change to the next commit (git add).
git.discard: Accessible label of a button that throws away the changes of one file. {{path}} is the file.
git.stage: Accessible label. Stage means add to the next commit.
git.unstage: Accessible label. Unstage removes a file from the next commit.
git.commitStaged: Button that commits only staged files.
git.currentBranch: Badge on the branch that is checked out. Lowercase.
git.switchBranch: Button that checks out a branch.
git.checkOut: Git verb: switch to a remote branch.
git.stashChanges: Button and heading that set uncommitted changes aside.
git.applyStash: Applies a stash and keeps it.
git.popStash: Applies a stash and deletes it.
git.restoreVersion: Button that replaces a file with an older version.
git.ours: Merge conflict side: the version from the current branch.
git.theirs: Merge conflict side: the version from the branch being merged.
git.acceptOurs: Resolves a conflict by keeping our side.
git.acceptTheirs: Resolves a conflict by keeping their side.
git.acceptBoth: Resolves a conflict by keeping both sides.
git.result: Heading of the merged result in the conflict editor.
git.reset: Button that restores the conflict editor to its start.
git.markResolved: Button that marks a conflicted file as resolved.
git.deletedSide: Shown in the conflict editor when one side deleted the file.
git.createPullRequest: Opens the pull request page on the code host in the web browser.
gitSession.dropStashConfirm: Confirm button of the stash deletion dialog.
